sentences.zh: 英国曾以工业力量的强大彻底革新了未来。

sentences.zh: 但现在，你可以借助 Hive 的力量，改变你自己的能源未来并掌握主动权。

sentences.en: Hive makes the most of the sun, with solar panels turning sunlight into greener electricity and enabling you to sell excess back to the grid.
sentences.zh: Hive 充分利用了太阳能，其太阳能电池板能将阳光转化为更环保的电力，并使你能够将多余的电量卖回给电网。

sentences.zh: 他们的热泵从空气中汲取热量，并将其精确保持在你想要的位置。

sentences.en: No smoke, no waste.
sentences.zh: 没有烟雾，没有浪费。

sentences.en: Hive's EV charger lets your car charge quietly overnight, recharging while you do too.
sentences.zh: Hive 的电动汽车充电器可以让你的汽车在夜间安静充电，在你休息的同时也为主力充电。

sentences.en: Hive brings it all together, heating, charging and solar, managed from one simple app in a quiet revolution.
sentences.zh: Hive 将供暖、充电和太阳能融为一体，在一场安静的变革中通过一个简单的应用程序进行管理。

sentences.en: In the long history of power, Hive helps you finally know yours.

sentences.zh: 前往 Hivehome.com 了解更多信息。

sentences.zh: 需视实地勘测和适用情况而定。

sentences.en: Hive app compatible with selected technology.
sentences.zh: Hive 应用程序兼容指定技术。

sentences.en: Paid for surplus requires SEG tariff.
sentences.zh: 出售剩余电量需要使用 SEG 费率。

sentences.en: Some of the reported clues must be received with caution.
sentences.zh: 一些流传的线索必须谨慎对待。

sentences.en: No end of stories are rife in the neighbourhood, told with an air of circumstantiality, which on examination proves to be utterly baseless.
sentences.zh: 街坊邻里间流传着无数的故事，讲得绘声绘色、有鼻子有眼，但经调查却完全毫无根据。

sentences.en: Almost the sole testimony which seems to have any bearing on the affair is that given by a young woman named Pannier, who sells roasted chestnuts at the corner of Widegate Street,
sentences.zh: 几乎唯一与本案有关的证词是一位名叫帕尼尔的年轻女子提供的，她在怀特盖特街拐角处卖烤栗子，

sentences.en: a narrow thoroughfare about two minutes' walk from the crime.
sentences.zh: 那是一条距离案发地点步行约两分钟的狭窄街道。

sentences.en: Mrs. Pannier is reported to have stated that shortly after noon yesterday, a man dressed like a gentleman said to her, I suppose you've heard about the murder in Dorset Street?
sentences.zh: 据报道，帕尼尔太太称，昨天中午过后不久，一个装扮得像绅士的男子对她说：“我想你听说多塞特街的谋杀案了吧？”

sentences.en: And when she replied that she was aware of it, he said, I know more about it than you.
sentences.zh: 当她回答说她知道此事时，他说：“我知道的内情比你更多。”

sentences.en: He then proceeded down Sandy's Row, a narrow thoroughfare which cuts across Widegate Street, looking back as if to see whether he was watched.
sentences.zh: 随后，他沿着桑迪罗（一条穿过怀特盖特街的狭窄街道）走去，不时回头张望，仿佛在查看是否有人监视。

sentences.en: Mrs. Pannier described this person as a man about 5 foot 6 inches high, with a black moustache and wearing a black silk hat, dark coat and speckled trousers.
sentences.zh: 帕尼尔太太将此人描述为身高约 5 英尺 6 英寸、留着黑色小胡子、头戴黑色丝绸礼帽、身穿深色外套和斑点长裤的男子。

sentences.en: He carried a black shiny bag, about 18 inches long and a foot deep.
sentences.zh: 他提着一个黑色的闪亮包，长约 18 英寸，深约 1 英尺。

sentences.en: It will be remembered that this description agrees fairly well with a personage previously described, and that the black bag has more than once figured in the evidence given.
sentences.zh: 值得一提的是，这个描述与先前描述的一个人物相当吻合，而且那个黑包在之前的证据中已不止一次出现过。

sentences.en: So that was the Daily Telegraph on the 10th of November, 1888.
sentences.zh: 以上就是 1888 年 11 月 10 日《每日电讯报》的内容。

sentences.en: It was following up its reports on a hideous discovery made the day before in Miller's Court, which was a small paved yard off Dorset Street in Spitalfields.
sentences.zh: 它当时正在跟进报道前一天在斯皮塔菲尔兹多塞特街旁一个小铺砌庭院米勒斯庭院中发现的一起骇人听闻的命案。

sentences.en: Now, we finished our previous episode in Miller's Court, number 13, with a terrible discovery.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们在上一集的结尾来到了米勒斯庭院 13 号，迎来了这个可怕的发现。

sentences.en: But just before we get into that discovery, let's talk a bit about Miller's Court and Dorset Street, Tom, because Dorset Street was notorious, wasn't it,
sentences.zh: 但在我们深入探讨那个发现之前，汤姆，让我们先来谈谈米勒斯庭院和多塞特街，因为多塞特街是出了名的，对吧，

sentences.en: as probably the worst street in London.
sentences.zh: 可以说是伦敦最糟糕的街道。

sentences.en: Yes, that is its reputation.
sentences.zh: 是的，它的名声确实如此。

sentences.en: And Miller's Court was one of a number of yards that kind of stretched off Dorset Street that had helped to give it that reputation.
sentences.zh: 而米勒斯庭院是多塞特街延伸出的众多庭院之一，这也正是它恶名远扬的原因所在。

sentences.en: And since the layout of Miller's Court is quite important to understanding the episodes that we're going to be describing in the next 20 or so minutes,
sentences.zh: 鉴于米勒斯庭院的布局对于理解我们在接下来大约二十分钟里要描述的案情非常重要，

sentences.en: let's give a description of it.
sentences.zh: 让我们来描述一下它的样貌。

sentences.en: So Miller's Court is accessed by a narrow, covered alley that leads off Dorset Street into what had once been a garden,
sentences.zh: 米勒斯庭院的入口是一条狭窄的有顶小巷，从多塞特街通往一个曾经的花园，

sentences.en: but has since been lined on either side of the walls of the garden with dilapidated two-story buildings.
sentences.zh: 但此后花园墙壁的两侧都盖满了破旧的两层楼建筑。

sentences.en: So it is very claustrophobic.
sentences.zh: 所以这里非常幽闭压抑。

sentences.en: It's very airless.
sentences.zh: 空气很不流通。

sentences.en: And even by day, it is shrouded in a kind of Stygian gloom.
sentences.zh: 甚至在白天，它也笼罩在一片冥河般的阴暗之中。

sentences.en: There are three privies that are set against the back wall.
sentences.zh: 后墙边设有三个厕所。

sentences.en: So you probably don't want to be caught short in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能不会想在半夜突然内急。

sentences.en: There is also a single gas lamp next to where the covered passageway from Dorset Street joins the yard.
sentences.zh: 从多塞特街通往庭院的有顶通道交汇处旁边，还立着一盏燃气路灯。

sentences.en: So if you come out from that covered passageway by night, it will be dark, but you will step out into a kind of flickering light from the gas lamp.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在夜间从那条有顶通道走出来，周围虽然昏暗，但你会步入燃气路灯发出的闪烁光芒中。

sentences.en: And that means that anyone who is emerging from the passageway, you know, people who are looking out from one of the windows, you know, the upper windows around the garden,
sentences.zh: 这意味着任何从通道里走出来的人，你知道的，那些从花园周围的某个窗户（比如上层窗户）往外看的人，

sentences.en: they would be able to see whoever was stepping out of the passageway.
sentences.zh: 他们都能看到任何走出通道的人。

sentences.en: If that person has stepped out of the passageway and he then turns sharp right,
sentences.zh: 如果这个人走出通道后紧接着向右急转弯，

sentences.en: he will then be confronted by a locked door.
sentences.zh: 他就会面对一扇锁着的门。

sentences.en: And this door in turn leads into number 13 Miller's Court and it is a converted parlour.
sentences.zh: 这扇门通往米勒斯庭院 13 号，这是一间改造过的会客室。

sentences.en: So just a single room and it's 10 feet by 12 feet.
sentences.zh: 所以只有一个房间，面积为 10 英尺乘 12 英尺。

sentences.en: So not large at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不大。

sentences.en: It's a very sparsely furnished.
sentences.zh: 里面的陈设非常简陋。

sentences.en: There's a bed.
sentences.zh: 有一张床。

sentences.en: There's a table.
sentences.zh: 有一张桌子。

sentences.en: There's a chair.
sentences.zh: 有一把椅子。

sentences.en: There's a wash stand.
sentences.zh: 有一个洗脸台。

sentences.en: There's a cupboard.
sentences.zh: 有一个碗柜。

sentences.en: There is also a fireplace and hung over the fireplace.
sentences.zh: 还有一个壁炉，壁炉上方挂着画。

sentences.en: There is a cheap print, the fisherman's widow.
sentences.zh: 那是一张廉价印刷品，画的是渔夫的寡妇。

sentences.en: Now, the person renting this room is a young woman, probably around 25 years old.
sentences.zh: 现在，租下这个房间的人是一个年轻女子，大约 25 岁左右。

sentences.en: And Dominic, you introduced us to her at the end of the last episode.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你在上一集的末尾向我们介绍了她。

sentences.en: She is called Mary Jane Kelly.
sentences.zh: 她叫玛丽·简·凯利。

sentences.en: And she owes her landlord 29 shillings, which is equivalent to six weeks rent.
sentences.zh: 她欠房东 29 先令，相当于六周的房租。

sentences.en: So she owes a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以她欠了很多钱。

sentences.en: She's badly in arrears.
sentences.zh: 她严重拖欠房租。

sentences.en: And we heard in our previous episode how on the morning of the 9th of November, 1888, her landlord, a shopkeeper called John McCarthy,
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集里听到，在 1888 年 11 月 9 日的早晨，她的房东、一个名叫约翰·麦卡锡的店主，

sentences.en: whose shop directly abuts the passageway that leads into Miller's Court.
sentences.zh: 他的店铺紧邻通往米勒斯庭院的通道。

sentences.en: So his shop is looking out onto Dorset Street.
sentences.zh: 所以他的店面正对着多塞特街。

sentences.en: And then the sidewall is part of what forms the passageway that leads into Miller's Court.
sentences.zh: 而侧墙构成了通往米勒斯庭院通道的一部分。

sentences.en: He's decided that, you know, six weeks back rent.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，你知道的，已经拖欠六周房租了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He needs the money.
sentences.zh: 他需要这笔钱。

sentences.en: It's time that she coughed up.
sentences.zh: 是时候让她付钱了。

sentences.en: And as you mentioned again in the previous episode, it's the day of the Lord's Mayor's show.
sentences.zh: 正如你在上一集再次提到的那样，那天正好是伦敦市长游行日。

sentences.en: And McCarthy is clearly anxious that Mary Jane might be going off to see the show.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡显然很担心玛丽·简可能会去看游行。

sentences.en: She talked about how she was looking forward to it.
sentences.zh: 她曾谈到自己是多么期待这一天。

sentences.en: And he wants to get the money out of her before she can go off and spend it on all the kind of festivities.
sentences.zh: 他想在她去把钱花在各种庆祝活动之前把钱要回来。

sentences.en: But obviously, Mary Jane is never going to get to the Lord Mayor's show.
sentences.zh: 但显然，玛丽·简永远也去不成市长游行了。

sentences.en: And in fact, a shadow is going to be cast over the Lord Mayor's show.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一片阴云将笼罩市长游行。

sentences.en: This day will not be remembered for the Lord Mayor parading through the streets of the city of London.
sentences.zh: 这一天不会因为伦敦市长在伦敦市的街道上游行而被铭记。

sentences.en: It will be remembered for unspeakable scene of horror.
sentences.zh: 它将被人们因那些无法言说的恐怖惨状而铭记。

sentences.en: John McCarthy, the shopkeeper, had sent his young assistant, Thomas Boyer, to knock on Mary Jane's locked door.
sentences.zh: 店主约翰·麦卡锡派他的年轻助手托马斯·博耶去敲玛丽·简反锁的门。

sentences.en: And as you described in the previous episode, he had seen something horrific.
sentences.zh: 正如你在上一集所描述的那样，他看到了可怕的景象。

sentences.en: And by the late morning, this is bringing police personnel crowding into Miller's Court.
sentences.zh: 到了深夜，大批警察涌入米勒斯庭院。

sentences.en: So they're coming into Dorset Street.
sentences.zh: 他们进入多塞特街。

sentences.en: They're crowding down that narrow alleyway.
sentences.zh: 他们挤进那条狭窄的小巷。

sentences.en: And they're filling this kind of squalid, cramped space.
sentences.zh: 他们挤满了这个肮脏逼仄的空间。

sentences.en: They're joined by the local police surgeon, Dr. Phillips, the Baxter, who we've been meeting periodically throughout this series.
sentences.zh: 当地警医菲利普斯医生也加入了他们的行列，还有巴克斯特，我们在本系列中不时见到他。

sentences.en: He has got there by 11.15 and 15 minutes later, he is joined by Inspector Abiline.
sentences.zh: 他在 11 点 15 分赶到了那里，15 分钟后，阿比林督察也赶到了。

sentences.en: Now, the door is locked and you might think that there was a certain degree of urgency about breaking into the room.
sentences.zh: 门是锁着的，你可能会觉得破门而入具有某种程度的紧迫性。

sentences.en: However, Phillips advises Abiline to wait for the bloodhounds to arrive.
sentences.zh: 然而，菲利普斯建议阿比林等警犬到来。

sentences.en: Dominic, you were talking about the bloodhounds.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你之前一直在谈论那些警犬。

sentences.en: Barnaby and Burgo or whatever they're called.
sentences.zh: 巴纳比和伯戈，还是叫什么名字来着。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's saying, well, you know, we don't want to go in and have human contact, disturb it.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，你知道的，我们不想进去留下人类接触的痕迹，从而破坏现场。

sentences.en: The dogs will be able to track down the killer if we leave it shut.
sentences.zh: 如果我们保持门窗紧闭，警犬就能追踪到凶手。

sentences.en: And so Abiline does as advised.
sentences.zh: 于是阿比林按建议行事。

sentences.en: But as you said, this plan for using the bloodhounds has kind of fallen through.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，这个使用警犬的计划最终泡汤了。

sentences.en: And their owner has decided to take them to a dog show instead.
sentences.zh: 它们的主人决定带它们去参加狗展。

sentences.en: So the bloodhounds never turn up.
sentences.zh: 所以警犬根本没有出现。

sentences.en: And finally, by half past one in the afternoon, Abiline has had enough of waiting.
sentences.zh: 最后，到了下午一点半，阿比林已经受够了等待。

sentences.en: And so he orders the door to be forced.
sentences.zh: 于是他下令强行破门。

sentences.en: And John McCarthy, he gets a pickaxe and he smashes the door in.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦卡锡拿来一把鹤嘴锄，把门砸开了。

sentences.en: Now, what do they find inside?
sentences.zh: 现在，他们在里面发现了什么？

sentences.en: They find that Mary Jane's clothes are neatly folded on the chair.
sentences.zh: 他们发现玛丽·简的衣服整齐地叠在椅子上。

sentences.en: In the fireplace,
sentences.zh: 在壁炉里，

sentences.en: there are the remains still of a fire that had clearly been so hot that it had burnt off the handle and spout of a tin kettle that had been placed next to the fireplace.
sentences.zh: 依然残留着炉火的余烬，这火显然烧得极旺，甚至把放在壁炉旁的一个锡水壶的手柄和壶嘴都烧掉了。

sentences.en: And lying on the bed is a body so hideously, so grotesquely mutilated that Dr. Phillips, when he spoke at the subsequent inquest, opted to suppress the full horror of the details.
sentences.zh: 躺在床上的是一具遭到如此骇人、如此怪诞肢解的尸体，以至于菲利普斯医生在随后的死因研讯中发言时，选择隐瞒了这些细节的全部恐怖之处。

sentences.en: And it's only in 1987 that a set of notes came to light that had been compiled by a second doctor, Thomas Bond, who also attended the murder scene that morning.
sentences.zh: 直到 1987 年，第二位医生托马斯·邦德整理的一组笔记才得以大白于天下，他当天早晨也去了谋杀现场。

sentences.en: And he'd arrived shortly after the door had been forced.
sentences.zh: 他在破门后不久就赶到了。

sentences.en: And he was very experienced in conducting postmorteMs.
sentences.zh: 他在进行尸检方面经验极其丰富。

sentences.en: And he recorded details in very kind of spare clinical prose.
sentences.zh: 他用非常精炼客观的临床笔触记录了细节。

sentences.en: And I will read from it now, but we've been issuing the warnings throughout the series that the details of the mutilations are horrific.
sentences.zh: 我现在将宣读其中的内容，但我们在整个系列中一直发出警告，肢解的细节极其恐怖。

sentences.en: And one of the things that people who've listened to them may have noticed is that the mutilations become more and more hideous as each murder is committed.
sentences.zh: 听过这些内容的人可能已经注意到的一点是，随着每起谋杀案的发生，肢解手法变得越来越骇人听闻。

sentences.en: And this is the culminating display of horror.
sentences.zh: 而这就是恐怖的最高峰。

sentences.en: There's clearly a sense that Mary Jane has been the victim of a kind of frenzied series of mutilations.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，玛丽·简是一系列疯狂虐杀肢解行径的受害者。

sentences.en: So with that warning, I will give you the details.
sentences.zh: 带着这个警告，我将向你们透露这些细节。

sentences.en: The whole of the surface of the abdomen and thighs was removed and the abdominal cavity emptied of its viscera.
sentences.zh: 腹部和大腿的整个表面都被剥除，腹腔内的内脏也被掏空。

sentences.en: The breasts were cut off, the arms mutilated by several jagged wounds,
sentences.zh: 乳房被割掉，手臂有多处锯齿状伤口残缺不全，

sentences.en: and the face hacked beyond recognition of the features and the tissues of the neck were severed all round down to the bone.
sentences.zh: 面部被砍得面目全非，无法辨认五官，颈部组织四周全被割断，直见白骨。

sentences.en: The uterus, the kidneys, one of the dismembered breasts had been placed under the head.
sentences.zh: 子宫、肾脏以及一个被割下的乳房被放在头部下方。

sentences.en: Then to quote Bond again, the other breast by the right foot, liver between the feet, the intestines by the right side and the spleen by the left side of the body.
sentences.zh: 接下来再次引用邦德的话：另一个乳房在右脚旁，肝脏在两脚之间，肠子在身体右侧，脾脏在身体左侧。

sentences.en: Blood, unsurprisingly, had soaked into the bed linen and into the mattress, and there was a still wet pool of blood that had spilled onto the floor.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，血液已经浸透了床单和床垫，地板上还留有一滩尚未干涸的血泊。

sentences.en: The heart had clearly been cut out and was nowhere to be found.
sentences.zh: 心脏显然被挖了出来，却不知去向。

sentences.en: And again, to quote Bond, the wall by the right side of the bed and in a line with the neck was marked by blood, which had struck it in a number of separate splashes.
sentences.zh: 再次引用邦德的话：床右侧、与颈部齐平的墙上有血迹，呈多处独立的飞溅状撞击在墙面上。

sentences.en: So Mary Jane Kelly is the first of the Ripper's victims to be murdered, not out in the streets or in a yard or something, but in a secluded private room.
sentences.zh: 因此，玛丽·简·凯利是开膛手第一个遇害的受害者，她不是在街头、庭院或其他地方遇害，而是在一个隐蔽的私人房间里。

sentences.en: And that's what's allowed the Ripper to take his time.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，开膛手才有时间从容行凶。

sentences.en: Yes, take his time and to indulge himself, I suppose, by going to the absolute extreme.
sentences.zh: 是的，从容不迫，我想他是在通过走向极致来放纵自己。

sentences.en: An extreme such that when the guy we mentioned last time, Joseph Barnett, a guy who's basically been Mary Jane Kelly's companion, who's been living with her,
sentences.zh: 这种极端程度使得我们上次提到的人——约瑟夫·巴内特，这个基本上一直是玛丽·简·凯利伴侣、与她同居的人，

sentences.en: and had lived with her until 10 days before the murder.
sentences.zh: 并且和她一起生活到谋杀案发生前 10 天的人，

sentences.en: When he was brought to identify her, she's no longer a recognizable human being.
sentences.zh: 当他被带来辨认尸体时，她已经不再是一个可以认得出的人类了。

sentences.en: It's a butcher's shambles.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像屠夫的肉案。

sentences.en: Yeah, he can identify by the hair and by the eyes, but nothing else.
sentences.zh: 是的，他只能通过头发和眼睛来辨认，别的什么都认不出来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's all that is left that enables him to identify her.
sentences.zh: 是的，只剩下这些能让他辨认出她了。

sentences.en: So we should put not just a face, but a life to Mary Jane Kelly.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不仅应该给玛丽·简·凯利一张面孔，更应该了解她的一生。

sentences.en: Who was she?
sentences.zh: 她究竟是谁？

sentences.en: You've said how her murder is kind of different to other ones because it's the only one that takes place in a private room.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说过，她的谋杀案与其他案件有些不同，因为这是唯一一起发生在私人房间里的谋杀案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's also significantly different to previous victims in that she is much younger.
sentences.zh: 她与以往受害者的另一个重大不同在于她年轻得多。

sentences.en: So we've said she's 25.
sentences.zh: 我们说过她 25 岁。

sentences.en: She's also reputedly very pretty.
sentences.zh: 据传她长得非常漂亮。

sentences.en: And we have no way of knowing because when you look at the photograph, you know, there's no trace of a human face there, really.
sentences.zh: 我们无从得知，因为当你看着那张照片时，你知道的，上面真的找不到人类面孔的痕迹了。

sentences.en: You know, as we said, the Ripper had spared her eyes and had spared her hair.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，开膛手饶了她的眼睛和头发。

sentences.en: And these were the two physical attributes for which Mary Jane was particularly noted.
sentences.zh: 而这两点正是玛丽·简尤为引人注目的两个身体特征。

sentences.en: So someone described her as having blue eyes and a very fine head of hair, which reached nearly to her waiSt.
sentences.zh: 有人曾形容她有着一双蓝色的眼睛和一头垂至腰际的极好的长发。

sentences.en: Now, what color was her hair?
sentences.zh: 那么，她到底是什么发色？

sentences.en: Some said it was blonde.
sentences.zh: 有人说她是金发。

sentences.en: Others said it was chestnut.
sentences.zh: 也有人说是栗色。

sentences.en: One of her nicknames was Black Mary.
sentences.zh: 她的绰号之一是“黑玛丽”。

sentences.en: Another was Ginger.
sentences.zh: 另一个绰号是“金杰”（Ginger）。

sentences.en: And it may seem odd to be speculating about the color of her hair.
sentences.zh: 猜测她的发色可能显得有些奇怪。

sentences.en: But I do so because the confusion is typical of almost everything that we know about her life.
sentences.zh: 但我之所以这么做，是因为这种混乱几乎普遍存在于我们对她一生的所有了解之中。

sentences.en: Well, we know nothing, effectively, do we?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们实际上什么都不知道，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, we know very, very little.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们了解得非常非常少。

sentences.en: It's just a sort of hall of mirrors.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一座镜厅。

sentences.en: So we don't even know.
sentences.zh: 所以我们甚至无从得知。

sentences.en: I mean, it's often said that she was Irish, but we don't even know that she was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经常有人说她是爱尔兰人，但我们甚至不确定她真的是。

sentences.en: She might have been Welsh, right?
sentences.zh: 她也有可能是威尔士人，对吧？

sentences.en: So she claimed to have come from Ireland.
sentences.zh: 因此，她自称来自爱尔兰。

sentences.en: She claimed to come from Wales.
sentences.zh: 她又自称来自威尔士。

sentences.en: The story that she most regularly said was that her parents were Irish, but had moved to Wales when she was very young.
sentences.zh: 她最常说的一个说法是，她的父母是爱尔兰人，但在她很小的时候搬到了威尔士。

sentences.en: But it's striking that she had neither an Irish nor a Welsh accent.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊讶的是，她既没有爱尔兰口音，也没有威尔士口音。

sentences.en: And so it's possible that perhaps she had elocution lessons or perhaps she was never Irish or Welsh in the first place.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许她上过正音课，或者她根本就不是爱尔兰人或威尔士人。

sentences.en: And in fact, we can't even be sure that Mary Jane Kelly was her real name because it's exactly the kind of name that someone pretending to be Irish would come up with.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们甚至无法确定玛丽·简·凯利是不是她的真名，因为这正是那种假装自己是爱尔兰人的人会起的名字。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And to quote Hallie Rubenhold in whose book, The Five, you know, she gives very detailed accounts of the lives of the other victims, all of them expertly sourced,
sentences.zh: 正如哈莉·鲁本霍德在她的书《五人》中所写的那样，你知道的，书中对其他受害者的生平有非常详细的记录，所有这些记录都经过了专家的考证，

sentences.en: kind of drawing on all kinds of written material.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上借鉴了各种书面资料。

sentences.en: But she says of Mary Jane Kelly, not a single statement made by her about her life prior to her arrival in London has ever been verified.
sentences.zh: 但她对玛丽·简·凯利的评价是：关于她抵达伦敦之前的生平，她所说的话没有一句得到过证实。

sentences.en: You know, people have crawled over the records.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们把档案都翻了个底朝天。

sentences.en: They've never found anything.
sentences.zh: 却什么也没找到。

sentences.en: So we don't know, for example, what class she's from, what her social status is, do we?
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我们不知道她出身于什么阶层，她的社会地位是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Because Joseph Barnett would read her stories about the Rippers' crimes, which suggests that she's illiterate.
sentences.zh: 因为约瑟夫·巴内特会给她读关于开膛手罪行的故事，这表明她是个文盲。

sentences.en: But other people who knew her said, and I quote, an excellent scholar and an artist of no mean degree.
sentences.zh: 但其他认识她的人却说——我引用一下——“她是一位极佳的学者，也是一位相当出色的艺术家。”

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So are people making stuff up or is she herself not telling people the truth about her life?
sentences.zh: 所以，是人们在胡编乱造，还是她自己没有对别人说实话？

sentences.en: So, for example, she says, doesn't she, that her father had been a Welsh steelworks foreman.
sentences.zh: 比如，她说过她父亲曾是威尔士钢铁厂的工头，不是吗？

sentences.en: She says she's got a brother in the Scots guards, but there's no evidence that either of those things are true at all.
sentences.zh: 她说她在苏格兰卫队有一个兄弟，但没有证据表明这两件事有任何一件是真的。

sentences.en: And she wouldn't be the only person.
sentences.zh: 而且她并不是唯一这样的人。

sentences.en: You know, Elizabeth Stride made up stories about herself as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，伊丽莎白·斯特赖德也编造过关于她自己的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not an uncommon thing to do if you've fallen down to the bottom that you take refuge in fantasies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你已经落魄到了社会底层，通过幻想来寻求庇护并不是什么罕见的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, but there are kind of substantiating records in Sweden that enable researchers to work out what her early years might have been like.
sentences.zh: 是的，但在瑞典有一些佐证记录，能让研究人员推测出她早年生活可能是怎样的。

sentences.en: We don't have those with Mary Jane.
sentences.zh: 而我们在玛丽·简身上没有这些记录。

sentences.en: For instance, Mary Jane claims that she had married.
sentences.zh: 例如，玛丽·简声称她曾结过婚。

sentences.en: Again, there's no record of this whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 同样，没有任何关于这方面的记录。

sentences.en: As for her career, so those who knew her were agreed.
sentences.zh: 至于她的职业，认识她的人意见一致。

sentences.en: And again, this is a point of difference between her and the previous victiMs.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也是她与前几位受害者不同的一点。

sentences.en: She was what the police termed a common prostitute, i.e. someone who self-identified as such, whose career had always involved prostitution.
sentences.zh: 她就是警察所说的“普通妓女”，也就是那些自我认同为此身份、职业生涯一直涉及卖淫的人。

sentences.en: The early stories that she tells of her life as a prostitute in London are actually quite reminiscent of, you know, Emma Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 她讲述的早期在伦敦当妓女的经历，其实非常让人想起埃玛·汉密尔顿。

sentences.en: There's a kind of the quality of the country girl who comes to London and leads the high life effectively by being a courtesan for very wealthy men.
sentences.zh: 有一种纯真乡村女孩来到伦敦的特质，实际上是通过给极有钱的男人当交际花来过上流生活。

sentences.en: Like Zola's character Nana, which a lot of people would have been familiar with at the time.
sentences.zh: 就像左拉笔下的娜娜，当时很多人对这个角色都很熟悉。

sentences.en: Yes, or Skittles, with her very tight writing habit.
sentences.zh: 是的，或者像穿着紧身骑马装的斯基特斯。

sentences.en: And so Mary Jane tells stories about how she had made a great success for herself in a very, very upmarket brothel in Knightsbridge,
sentences.zh: 因此，玛丽·简讲述了她是多么成功地在骑士桥的一家非常非常高级的妓院里混得风生水起，

sentences.en: which is one of the kind of the classiest areas of the West End.
sentences.zh: 那是西区最高档的地区之一。

sentences.en: That she had had beautiful dresses, that she'd ridden around in a carriage, that she'd eaten oysters in fashionable restaurants, all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 她说自己曾拥有漂亮的裙子，坐着马车到处兜风，在时尚的餐馆里吃生蚝，诸如此类。

sentences.en: That in her own words, she had led the life of a lady.
sentences.zh: 用她自己的话说，她过着贵妇般的生活。

sentences.en: And perhaps a marker of that is that Mary Jane, she seems to have decided wasn't good enough for her.
sentences.zh: 也许这的一个标志就是，玛丽·简似乎觉得这个名字配不上自己。

sentences.en: And so she starts referring to herself as Marie Jeannette.
sentences.zh: 于是她开始称自己为玛丽·珍妮特（Marie Jeannette）。

sentences.en: And the hint of the French is telling because she also told a story about how she had been taken to Paris by, quote unquote, a gentleman.
sentences.zh: 这种法式风味暗示了某些东西，因为她还讲过一个故事，说她曾被一个“绅士”（姑且这么称呼）带去了巴黎。

sentences.en: But she had only stayed there, she said, at fortnight and then returned to London.
sentences.zh: 但她说她只在那里呆了两周，然后就回到了伦敦。

sentences.en: But when she comes back to London, she doesn't go back to the West End.
sentences.zh: 然而当她回到伦敦时，她并没有回到西区。

sentences.en: She doesn't go back to her life of carriages and beautiful dresses and oysters.
sentences.zh: 她没有回到坐马车、穿漂亮裙子、吃生蚝的生活。

sentences.en: She goes to the East End.
sentences.zh: 她去了东区。

sentences.en: And that's puzzling.
sentences.zh: 这很让人费解。

sentences.en: What had changed in those two weeks?
sentences.zh: 那两周里究竟发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: And the stories that she tells are kind of full of melodrama.
sentences.zh: 她讲述的故事充满了情节剧的色彩。

sentences.en: She strongly implies that she's in the East End because she's hiding from people who are out to get her.
sentences.zh: 她强烈暗示自己之所以在东区，是因为她在躲避那些想要对她不利的人。

sentences.en: But who?
sentences.zh: 但会是谁呢？

sentences.en: She launches an abortive attempt to liberate a chest full of dresses that she says is in a house in Knightsbridge.
sentences.zh: 她曾试图取回一箱子裙子，说那是放在骑士桥的一栋房子里，但这次尝试无果而终。

sentences.en: But nothing really comes of it.
sentences.zh: 不过也没什么实质结果。

sentences.en: And she also says that a man has appeared near to where she's living, claiming to be her father, but wasn't hunting her down.
sentences.zh: 她还说，她住处附近出现了一个男人，自称是她的父亲，但并非在搜寻她。

sentences.en: There's no real evidence for any of this beyond what she herself is reporting.
sentences.zh: 除了她自己的说辞之外，没有真实的证据支持这些说法。

sentences.en: Well, I made the comparison with Zola's novel Nana about a courtesan in Paris.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我把她与左拉关于巴黎交际花的小说《娜娜》进行了对比。

sentences.en: And this does all feel too literary, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这一切确实显得太文学化了，不是吗？

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 有点像。

sentences.en: It feels like the kind of story that you would make up about kind of, you know, mysterious gentleman kind of rakes taking you to Paris.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像你会编造的那种故事，关于什么神秘的绅士或浪子把你带去了巴黎。

sentences.en: The newspapers in the 1880s are full of stories about so-called white slavery.
sentences.zh: 19世纪80年代的报纸上到处都是关于所谓“白奴”的故事。

sentences.en: You know, girls who've been kidnapped and used as sex slaves.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，女孩被绑架并被当作性奴隶。

sentences.en: I think that she's making this stuff up because it's a good story.
sentences.zh: 我认为她是在胡编乱造，因为这故事很精彩。

sentences.en: It makes her feel important.
sentences.zh: 这让她觉得自己很重要。

sentences.en: It makes her customers feel that she is important.
sentences.zh: 也让她的客户觉得她很重要。

sentences.en: You know, it's better than the truth, which is that she's a nobody.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这总比真相要好，真相是她只是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And of course, she is selling herself.
sentences.zh: 而且当然，她在兜售自己。

sentences.en: And if you can make yourself seem glamorous, then, you know, you're likely to create a market for yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你能让自己看起来光鲜亮丽，那么你就有可能为自己创造一个市场。

sentences.en: But obviously Miller's court, which she'd moved into by March 1888.
sentences.zh: 但显然，她到1888年3月搬进去的米勒斯庭院（Miller's Court），

sentences.en: I mean, it is the opposite of glamorous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那简直与光鲜亮丽截然相反。

sentences.en: But I think she moves in there and into Whitechapel more generally, because by this point, she's found herself a steady partner and seems to have given up on the prostitution.
sentences.zh: 但我认为她搬到那里以及更广泛的白教堂地区，是因为到这个时候，她已经找到了一个稳定的伴侣，并且似乎已经放弃了卖淫。

sentences.en: She stopped the soliciting.
sentences.zh: 她不再拉客了。

sentences.en: And this partner, we've already mentioned him.
sentences.zh: 而这个伴侣，我们之前已经提到过了。

sentences.en: He's Joseph Barnett.
sentences.zh: 他就是约瑟夫·巴内特。

sentences.en: This is the guy who will identify her in due course by her eyes and her hair.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个后来通过她的眼睛和头发来辨认出她尸体的人。

sentences.en: And he was a porter at Billingsgate Fish Market.
sentences.zh: 他是比灵斯门鱼市的一名搬运工。

sentences.en: And like Mary Jane, he had blue eyes and he was of Irish extraction.
sentences.zh: 和玛丽·简一样，他有蓝眼睛，也有爱尔兰血统。

sentences.en: If Mary Jane really was of Irish extraction.
sentences.zh: 如果玛丽·简真的有爱尔兰血统的话。

sentences.en: And Barnett was very, very keen on her, very fond of her and clearly wanted to make a go of things.
sentences.zh: 巴内特非常非常喜欢她，对她感情很深，显然想和她好好过日子。

sentences.en: He treated her as his wife.
sentences.zh: 他把她当成自己的妻子对待。

sentences.en: That's why she gives up soliciting.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么她放弃了拉客。

sentences.en: They're essentially living as a married couple.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上像已婚夫妇一样生活在一起。

sentences.en: But by the autumn of 1888, their relationship is getting slightly rocky.
sentences.zh: 但到了1888年秋天，他们的关系开始有点动摇。

sentences.en: In July, Barnett had lost his job in the fish market and he gets kind of occasional work as a labourer, but not a regular income.
sentences.zh: 7月份时，巴内特失去了鱼市的工作，虽然他偶尔做点零工当力工，但没有稳定的收入。

sentences.en: And so there's a need to pay the rent.
sentences.zh: 因此这就产生了支付房租的需求。

sentences.en: And so Mary Jane returns to soliciting on the streets.
sentences.zh: 于是玛丽·简重操旧业，回到街头拉客。

sentences.en: And adding to the strain that I think this obviously places on their relationship is the fact that she is famously warm-hearted.
sentences.zh: 我认为这显然给他们的关系带来了压力，除此之外还有一个事实：她出了名的热心肠。

sentences.en: She's terribly popular among her fellow workers on the street.
sentences.zh: 她在街头同行中极其受欢迎。

sentences.en: And I think more generally, very kind-hearted.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为更普遍地说，她非常善良。

sentences.en: And she's always inviting fellow prostitutes, if it's cold or wet or whatever, to come back and share the room.
sentences.zh: 每当遇到寒冷、下雨或其他什么情况，她总是邀请同行的妓女回来分享她的房间。

sentences.en: Barnett's not terribly happy about this, is he?
sentences.zh: 巴内特对此很不高兴，对吧？

sentences.en: He finds it very annoying.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这非常烦人。

sentences.en: And actually, he ends up moving out of Miller's court.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他最终搬出了米勒斯庭院。

sentences.en: So not that long before the, what, about 10 days before the murder, he's moved out.
sentences.zh: 就在谋杀发生前不久，大概也就是谋杀前10天左右，他搬出去了。

sentences.en: They have a massive row and he kind of stalks off.
sentences.zh: 他们大吵了一架，他气冲冲地走了。

sentences.en: But he can't bear to go too far, so he finds a room very close to her.
sentences.zh: 但他又舍不得走太远，于是在离她很近的地方找了个房间。

sentences.en: And over the week that follows, he comes back and he's clearly trying to patch things up with her.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的一个星期里，他回来了，显然是在试图修复和她的关系。

sentences.en: He clearly wants to get back with her.
sentences.zh: 他显然想和她复合。

sentences.en: And he comes back to her to see her on the evening of the 8th of November.
sentences.zh: 他在11月8日傍晚回来见她。

sentences.en: He does this kind of in the early evening.
sentences.zh: 他是在傍晚时分去的。

sentences.en: And a neighbour of Mary Jane's, so in Miller's court, reported later that they seem to be on the best of terMs.
sentences.zh: 米勒斯庭院里玛丽·简的一位邻居后来报告说，他们当时关系看起来非常好。

sentences.en: And Barnett himself, when he was interviewed by the police, he said, I told her that I had no work and that I had nothing to give her, for which I was very sorry.
sentences.zh: 巴内特本人在接受警方盘问时说：“我告诉她我没有工作，也没有什么可以给她，对此我感到非常抱歉。”

sentences.en: He then left around 7.45.
sentences.zh: 然后他在7点45分左右离开。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he's sorry, why?
sentences.zh: 他为什么要抱歉？

sentences.en: Because she needs money.
sentences.zh: 因为她需要钱。

sentences.en: Well, of course, we know she needs money because we know that she's behind on the rent by six weeks, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道她需要钱，因为我们知道她的房租已经拖欠了六周，对吧？

sentences.en: So if Barnett doesn't have the money to give her, where is she going to get the money to pay the landlord?
sentences.zh: 所以如果巴内特没有钱给她，她要从哪里弄钱来付给房东呢？

sentences.en: There are various kind of interpretations of McCarthy's character.
sentences.zh: 人们对麦卡锡（McCarthy）的性格有各种各样的解读。

sentences.en: So Halley in The Five is very down on him, calls him a bully and implies that he's always trying to extort money out of him.
sentences.zh: 比如《五人》中的哈莉对他的评价很低，称他为恶霸，并暗示他总是试图勒索钱财。

sentences.en: Others say that he was quite fond of Mary Jane.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则说他对玛丽·简挺疼爱的。

sentences.en: And I guess that, you know, six weeks back rent is quite a lot because all the other women that we've been describing,
sentences.zh: 我想，拖欠六周房租其实挺多的，因为我们描述过的所有其他女性，

sentences.en: almost invariably, they're being turfed out of their bed because they don't have money to pay for a single night.
sentences.zh: 几乎无一例外，因为她们连住一个晚上的钱都拿不出来而被赶出了床位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Whereas Mary Jane is in her room and is there for six weeks.
sentences.zh: 而玛丽·简却能在她的房间里呆上六周。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But you can see why he, you know, maybe he's running out of patience.
sentences.zh: 但你可以理解为什么他，你知道的，也许他快失去耐心了。

sentences.en: Maybe he's trying to turn the screws.
sentences.zh: 也许他正在给对方施加压力。

sentences.en: And I think that that is clearly why that evening, despite the fact that the rain is very, very torrential,
sentences.zh: 我认为这显然就是为什么那天晚上，尽管外面下着倾盆大雨，

sentences.en: Mary Jane seems to have been desperate to solicit clients.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·简似乎仍然迫切地想要揽客。

sentences.en: After Joseph Burnett has gone, she clearly leaves her room and goes out into the streets and is trying to attract custom.
sentences.zh: 在约瑟夫·巴内特离开后，她显然离开了房间，走到街上试图招揽生意。

sentences.en: And we have two witnesses who would subsequently claim to have seen her with men that night.
sentences.zh: 我们有两位目击者后来声称当晚看到她和男人们在一起。

sentences.en: And the first of these is a man who is seen accompanying her into her room by someone who is looking down from one of the top stories around Miller's court.
sentences.zh: 其中第一位目击者是一个人，米勒斯庭院周围高层窗户上有人往下看，看到他正陪着她进入她的房间。

sentences.en: So he is lit by that gas lamp that we mentioned.
sentences.zh: 所以他被我们提到过的那盏煤气灯照亮了。

sentences.en: And he's described as having a thick, carot-y moustache.
sentences.zh: 据描述，他留着浓密的胡子，颜色呈胡萝卜色。

sentences.en: He's dressed in shabby, dark clothes.
sentences.zh: 他穿着破旧的深色衣服。

sentences.en: He's got a dark overcoat.
sentences.zh: 穿着一件深色过膝大衣。

sentences.en: He's got a black felt hat.
sentences.zh: 戴着一顶黑色毡帽。

sentences.en: And he is seen just before midnight.
sentences.zh: 人们看到他时正值午夜前不久。

sentences.en: He's going into the room with Mary Jane.
sentences.zh: 他正和玛丽·简一起走进房间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Mary Jane at the time was reportedly quite drunk.
sentences.zh: 据报道，玛丽·简当时喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: She was in a mood for an Irish ballad.
sentences.zh: 她正想听一首爱尔兰民谣。

sentences.en: And we know it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此心知肚明。

sentences.en: And the lyrics I find incredibly sad, kind of so full of pathos.
sentences.zh: 我发现其中的歌词极其悲伤，充满了哀婉动人的情感。

sentences.en: So she sang, scenes of my childhood arise before my gaze, bringing recollections of bygone happy days, when down in the meadow in childhood I would roam.
sentences.zh: 所以她唱道：“童年的景象浮现在我眼前，勾起了对过去快乐时光的回忆，当年童年时我在草地上漫步。如今那个温暖的老家里，已无人留下为我欢呼。”

sentences.en: No one's left to cheer me now within that good old home.
sentences.zh: 如今那个温暖的老家里，已无人留下为我欢呼。

sentences.en: So whoever she was, she'd clearly left her home behind.
sentences.zh: 所以无论她是谁，她显然已经抛弃了她的家园。

sentences.en: And she had no family that she would acknowledge or who would acknowledge her or maybe even knew where she was.
sentences.zh: 她没有她会承认的家人，也没有会承认她的家人，甚至可能没人知道她在哪里。

sentences.en: So there is a kind, I find, an incredible pathos about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这其中有一种令人难以置信的凄美。

sentences.en: And what about the second witness?
sentences.zh: 那第二位目击者呢？

sentences.en: So the second witness is an unemployed laborer called George Hutchinson.
sentences.zh: 第二位目击者是一个名叫乔治·哈utchinson（George Hutchinson）的失业零工。

sentences.en: He had a kind of a bit of a crush on Mary Jane, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他对玛丽·简有点迷恋，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he'd seen her before and would periodically give her money.
sentences.zh: 他以前见过她，并会定期给她钱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He doesn't have a job at the time.
sentences.zh: 他当时没有工作。

sentences.en: So when he runs into Mary Jane walking down Thrall Street around 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在凌晨两点左右遇到玛丽·简沿着索罗街走来时

sentences.en: And she asks him for money and he says, sorry, I'm skinned, haven't got anything, can't help.
sentences.zh: 而她向他要钱，他说，对不起，我口袋空空，什么也没有，帮不上忙。

sentences.en: And Hutchinson then says, after this exchange that Mary Jane had had with him, he had watched her be approached by a second man.
sentences.zh: 哈钦森随后说，在玛丽·简与他有过这段对话后，他看到另一个男人向她走近。

sentences.en: And this is a person who's pale-faced, according to Hutchinson, and very well-dressed.
sentences.zh: 根据哈钦森的说法，这个人脸色苍白，衣着十分考究。

sentences.en: He's wearing an Astrakhan coat.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一件阿斯特拉罕羔皮大衣。

sentences.en: And the two of them haggle.
sentences.zh: 两人讨价还价。

sentences.en: Terms are agreed.
sentences.zh: 双方达成了一致。

sentences.en: And Hutchinson then watches the two of them disappear off Dorset Street down the dark alleyway that leads into Miller's Court.
sentences.zh: 接着，哈钦森看着两人从多塞特街消失，走进了通往米勒法院的黑暗小巷。

sentences.en: Well, he gives a very detailed description, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他给出了非常详细的描述，不是吗？

sentences.en: So I'll just read it.
sentences.zh: 所以我就直接宣读了。

sentences.en: Light waistcoat, dark trousers, and a dark felt hat turned down in the middle.
sentences.zh: 浅色马甲，深色裤子，中间向下翻卷的深色毡帽。

sentences.en: Button boots and gaiters with white buttons.
sentences.zh: 系扣靴子和带有白色纽扣的护腿。

sentences.en: Wore a very thick gold chain, white linen collar.
sentences.zh: 戴着一条非常粗的金链子，白色亚麻衣领。

sentences.en: Black tie with horseshoe pin.
sentences.zh: 黑领带配马蹄形别针。

sentences.en: Respectable appearance.
sentences.zh: 外表体面。

sentences.en: Walked very sharp.
sentences.zh: 走路步伐极其利落。

sentences.en: Jewish appearance.
sentences.zh: 有犹太人的外貌特征。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he will then go on to give another, even more detailed description of this man.
sentences.zh: 他接着又对这个人进行了更详尽的描述。

sentences.en: And people may wonder, it's dark.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会觉得，当时天很黑。

sentences.en: They're standing in shadows.
sentences.zh: 他们站在阴影里。

sentences.en: How plausible is it that he would have seen every detail?
sentences.zh: 他怎么可能看清每一个细节？这可信吗？

sentences.en: And we will come to this in due course.
sentences.zh: 我们随后就会讲到这一点。

sentences.en: But just to finish detailing Hutchinson's evidence, he said that he'd waited by the entrance of Miller's Court for just under an hour.
sentences.zh: 不过，为了讲完哈钦森的证词，他说他在米勒法院入口处等了不到一个小时。

sentences.en: And that neither Mary Jane nor her client reappeared.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·简和她的客户都没有重新出现。

sentences.en: If he can be trusted, they had disappeared into her room around two o'clock.
sentences.zh: 如果他的话可信的话，他们大约在两点钟消失在她的房间里。

sentences.en: And he, again, if he's to be trusted, is the last witness to see her alive, but not perhaps the last to hear Mary Jane's voice.
sentences.zh: 如果他的话值得相信，他也是最后一个看到她活着的人，但也许不是最后一个听到玛丽·简声音的人。

sentences.en: Because there are two separate women.
sentences.zh: 因为有两个不同的女人。

sentences.en: And one of them is a woman called Elizabeth Prater, who is the lodger in the rooms directly above Mary Jane's room.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是叫伊丽莎白·普拉特的女人，她是玛丽·简房间正上方房间的房客。

sentences.en: And the other is a laundress called Sarah Lewis, who has been made homeless and is taking refuge with a couple on the room opposite 13 Miller Court across the courtyard.
sentences.zh: 另一个是一个叫莎拉·刘易斯的洗衣女工，她无家可归，正和庭院对面米勒法院13号对门的一对夫妇一起避难。

sentences.en: And both these women reported hearing screams of murder at around 4 a.m.
sentences.zh: 这两名妇女都报告说在凌晨4点左右听到过谋杀的尖叫声。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And listeners may be wondering, well, why didn't they do something about it?
sentences.zh: 听众可能会想，那他们为什么不采取点行动呢？

sentences.en: And in fact, the police asked exactly this question.
sentences.zh: 事实上，警方问的正是这个问题。

sentences.en: And Mrs. Prater said, she told the police, I did not take much notice of the cries as I frequently hear such cries.
sentences.zh: 普拉特太太说，她告诉警方，我没有太在意这些呼救声，因为我经常听到这样的叫喊。

sentences.en: And it is worth adding that the autopsy, the doctors who did that, the surgeons, they suggested that the likeliest time of death was around 4 a.m.
sentences.zh: 值得补充的是，验尸官、进行解剖的医生和外科医生表明，最可能的死亡时间是在凌晨4点左右。

sentences.en: Although if that's true, and George Hutchinson's story is true,
sentences.zh: 尽管如果这是真的，乔治·哈钦森的故事也是真的，

sentences.en: then that means there's been a two-hour interval between the killer going into the room and then the murder actually happening, which would be odd,
sentences.zh: 那就意味着凶手进入房间到谋杀实际发生之间有两个小时的间隔，这未免有些奇怪，

sentences.en: given that in every previous case, the Ripper has killed very quickly and efficiently.
sentences.zh: 考虑到在以往的每一个案件中，开膛手都下手极快且十分利落。

sentences.en: Now, I can understand the Ripper might want to be alone with the body to do his mutilations for hours.
sentences.zh: 现在，我能理解开膛手可能想独自与尸体待在一起几个小时来进行他的残害行为。

sentences.en: You know, what have they been doing for two hours?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们这两个小时都在干什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is never done before, before this killing.
sentences.zh: 这在这次谋杀之前是从来没有过的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So those two suspects who are seen with Mary Jane on the evening of her death, both of them have been identified as very strong candidates to have been the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 因此，在玛丽·简遇害当晚与她在一起的那两个嫌疑人，都被认定为极具可能是开膛手的嫌疑对象。

sentences.en: But I think actually neither of them necessarily are.
sentences.zh: 但我认为实际上他们两个都不一定是。

sentences.en: I think the guy with the carotene moustache, I mean, clearly, you know, he's going in at just after midnight.
sentences.zh: 我认为那个留着胡子的家伙，我的意思是，很显然，你知道的，他刚过午夜就进去了。

sentences.en: Mary Jane is desperate for large numbers of clients.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·简极度渴望有大量的客户。

sentences.en: It's perfectly possible that she did go out and maybe get this guy in the astrakhan coat.
sentences.zh: 完全有可能她确实出去了，并且可能把这个穿着阿斯特拉罕羔皮大衣的家伙带了进来。

sentences.en: And it's perfectly possible after that, that she went out and got someone else who might be the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，她完全有可能又出去了，并带进来了另一个人，而那个人可能是开膛手。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's not definitive.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是确凿的。

sentences.en: But whoever it was that ended up in that room with Mary Jane at around four o'clock in the morning, we know the upshot because we have described it in all its hideous detail.
sentences.zh: 但无论最后在凌晨四点左右和玛丽·简待在那个房间里的人是谁，我们都知道结果，因为我们已经对它进行了种种骇人听闻的详细描述。

sentences.en: And of course, it takes time for the examining surgeons to make sense of the horror.
sentences.zh: 当然，负责检查的外科医生需要时间来理清这恐怖的一幕。

sentences.en: And it's not until four o'clock in the afternoon that you can't recall it a body.
sentences.zh: 直到下午四点，你才能把尸体抬走。

sentences.en: The kind of the remains, the mangled remains of Mary Jane Kelly is removed from her room.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·简·凯利支离破碎的遗体从她的房间里被抬了出来。

sentences.en: And by this point, a car with a tarpaulin cover has arrived and is waiting outside the dark passageway that leads out into Dorset Street.
sentences.zh: 此时，一辆盖着防水布的马车已经抵达，正停在通往多塞特街的黑暗通道外面。

sentences.en: And by now, as is becoming commonplace with a Jack the Ripper murder,
sentences.zh: 到了现在，正如针对开膛手杰克谋杀案的那样，这已经司空见惯了，

sentences.en: huge numbers of people are gathering outside the scene of the crime and they're swelled by the fact that it's the Lord Mayor's show.
sentences.zh: 大量的人群聚集在犯罪现场外，由于当天正好是伦敦市长巡游，人数更是急剧膨胀。

sentences.en: And as the news of the murder has swept the crowds in the city of London,
sentences.zh: 随着谋杀案的消息席卷了伦敦城的人群，

sentences.en: so huge numbers have have left the route of the procession and started flocking into Whitechapel in a kind of state of mass hysteria.
sentences.zh: 大量的人离开了游行路线，开始涌入白教堂，处于一种集体歇斯底里的状态。

sentences.en: And when Mary Jane's body is brought out by the police and laid onto the cart, the police who are keeping order in Dorset Street have to form a cordon to hold the crowds back.
sentences.zh: 当玛丽·简的尸体被警察抬出来并放到马车上时，在多塞特街维持秩序的警察不得不组成警戒线来阻挡人群。

sentences.en: And a journalist from The Times the next morning reported on this.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，《泰晤士报》的一名记者对此进行了报道。

sentences.en: The crowd was of the humblest class, but the demeanor of the poor people was all that could be desired.
sentences.zh: 人群来自最卑微的阶层，但穷人们的表现无可挑剔。

sentences.en: Ragged caps were doffed and slatternly looking women shed tears as the shell covered with a ragged looking cloth was placed in the van.
sentences.zh: 当盖着破旧布料的灵柩被放入厢式货车时，人们脱下了破烂的帽子，衣衫褴褛的妇女流下了眼泪。

sentences.en: And then the inquests are held and 10 days later, when Mary Kelly's funeral is held at Shoreditch Church, no family member could be found to attend the funeral.
sentences.zh: 随后举行了死因研讯，10天后，当玛丽·凯利的葬礼在肖尔迪奇教堂举行时，竟然找不到任何家属来参加葬礼。

sentences.en: So she remains a mystery.
sentences.zh: 所以她依然是一个谜。

sentences.en: Instead, riding in the two mourning carriages that are accompanying the hearse to the Catholic cemetery in Leightonstone are six women who had known her.
sentences.zh: 相反，坐在护送灵车前往莱顿斯通天主教公墓的两辆灵车里的，是六个曾经认识她的女人。

sentences.en: And these include Elizabeth Prater and Sarah Lewis, the two women who had heard the cry of murder at 4 a.m.
sentences.zh: 其中包括伊丽莎白·普拉特和莎拉·刘易斯，这两个在凌晨4点听到谋杀呼喊声的女人。

sentences.en: A mourner representing John McCarthy, her landlord, and Joseph Barnett.
sentences.zh: 还有代表她的房东约翰·麦卡锡的哀悼者，以及约瑟夫·巴尼特。

sentences.en: And it was Barnett who had insisted that she should be buried as a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 正是巴尼特坚持要将她按天主教仪式安葬。

sentences.en: So I think clearly he believed that she was Irish because obviously, you know, if she'd been Welsh, he would have directed her to a Methodist chapel or something.
sentences.zh: 所以我想他显然相信她是爱尔兰人，因为很明显，你知道的，如果她是威尔士人，他就会把她送到卫理公会教堂或类似的地方了。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: And it's also Barnett who insists that her name on both the kind of the brass coffin plate and on her gravestone should read Marie Jeannette Kelly.
sentences.zh: 而且也正是巴尼特坚持要在黄铜棺铭牌和墓碑上把她的名字写成玛丽·珍妮特·凯利。

sentences.en: So the glamorous French sophisticated name that she would have always wanted, right?
sentences.zh: 也就是她一直渴望得到的那个光鲜迷人的法国高级名字，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, she was clearly a woman who enjoyed attention and she certainly gets attention at her funeral because huge crowds gather to watch the procession and women sob.
sentences.zh: 是的，她显然是一个喜欢引人注目的女人，在她的葬礼上她也确实引人注目，因为大批群众聚集观看游行队伍，女人们啜泣着。

sentences.en: And again, men are doffing their caps as the open hearse passes by.
sentences.zh: 同样，当敞篷灵车驶过时，男人们也纷纷脱帽致敬。

sentences.en: And as you suggest, Dominic, in death, she's become what I think she had always dreamed of being, which is essentially the heroine of a melodrama,
sentences.zh: 正如你所暗示的，多米尼克，在死后，她成为了我认为她一直梦想成为的人，也就是情节剧的女主角，

sentences.en: no matter how dark and terrible the melodrama has actually turned out to be.
sentences.zh: 不管这个情节剧实际上变得多么黑暗和可怕。

sentences.en: And bystanders weep at the thought of the fate that has befallen her.
sentences.zh: 旁观者为降临在她身上的命运感到心碎落泪。

sentences.en: And they pray to God to forgive her and they are, I think, hailing her,
sentences.zh: 他们祈求上帝宽恕她，我想，他们是在欢呼，

sentences.en: enshrining her as a symbol of their collective defiance of the fiend who had brought her to her terrible doom.
sentences.zh: 将她奉为他们集体反抗那个把她带向可怕厄运的恶魔的象征。

sentences.en: Well, you call him a fiend, but of course, Jack the Ripper was all too human.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你称他为恶魔，但当然，开膛手杰克也完全是个人。

sentences.en: And after the break, we will come back to look at what people make of the Ripper now that he has struck again and the impact that it has on popular culture.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我们将回过头来看看人们现在如何看待开膛手，以及他再次作案对流行文化产生的影响。

sentences.en: Because, of course, this is the age of Sherlock Holmes, of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，这是福尔摩斯、《化身博士》的时代。

sentences.en: Now, two months before the murder of Mary Jane Kelly, on the 8th of September, the editor of the Pall Mall Gazette,
sentences.zh: 现在，在玛丽·简·凯利遇害两个月前，即9月8日，《帕尔马报》的主编，

sentences.en: W.T.
sentences.zh: W.T.

sentences.en: Stead.
sentences.zh: 斯特德。

sentences.en: William Thomas Stead.
sentences.zh: 威廉·托马斯·斯特德。

sentences.en: He had written an absolutely ferocious attack on the police.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一篇极其猛烈的抨击警察的文章。

sentences.en: And the headline was,
sentences.zh: 头条新闻是，

sentences.en: Another murder and more to follow.
sentences.zh: 又是一起谋杀案，而且还会有更多。

sentences.en: And Stead said,
sentences.zh: 斯特德说，

sentences.en: The triumphant success with which the Metropolitan Police have suppressed all political meetings in Trafalgar Square contrasts strangely with their absolute failure to prevent the most brutal kind of murder in Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 大都会警察局在特拉法加广场取缔所有政治集会的辉煌成功，与他们无力阻止白教堂最残酷的谋杀案形成了鲜明而怪异的对比。

sentences.en: And this is a question that people are asking more and more, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们越来越多地提出的问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Why have the police,
sentences.zh: 为什么警察，

sentences.en: who have been so effective at doing the government's bidding at clearing homeless people out of Trafalgar Square on Bloody Sunday in 1887 and beating up demonstrators and whatnot,
sentences.zh: 他们在执行政府命令时如此高效——在1887年血腥星期日清空特拉法加广场的无家可归者、殴打示威者等方面驾轻就熟，

sentences.en: they're so good at this, but they cannot solve the murders of Polly Nichols and Annie Chapman and, of course, the subsequent Ripper victiMs.
sentences.zh: 他们在这方面如此在行，却无法破获波莉·尼科尔斯、安妮·查普曼的谋杀案，当然，还有随后的一系列开膛手受害者的案件。

sentences.en: And we're focusing on Stead, aren't we, in the Pall Mall Gazette, because this is a man whose career is at its absolute zenith at the time of the Ripper murders.
sentences.zh: 我们把焦点放在《帕尔马报》的斯特德身上，是因为在开膛手谋杀案发生时，这个人正处于其职业生涯的绝对巅峰。

sentences.en: And he has established in many ways the context in which the Ripper murders are understood.
sentences.zh: 他在很大程度上确立了人们理解开膛手谋杀案的背景。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's been kind of appearing throughout our series so far,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他到目前为止在我们的系列节目中经常出现，

sentences.en: but I think it's good to kind of dive and have a closer look at him because he has an absolute genius for campaigning journalism.
sentences.zh: 但我认为深入了解他并仔细观察他是很好的，因为他在开展政治活动新闻报道方面有着无与伦比的天才。

sentences.en: He's the effective inventor of Britain's tabloid press, and he is, I think, in a sense,
sentences.zh: 他实际上是英国小报新闻的鼻祖，而且我认为从某种意义上说，

sentences.en: the most interesting contemporary commentator on the series of murders that are taking place.
sentences.zh: 他是正在发生的一系列谋杀案中最有趣的当代评论员。

sentences.en: And he's been the editor of the Pall Mall Gazette since 1883, and over the course of his term in the editor's chair,
sentences.zh: 他自1883年起担任《帕尔马报》的主编，在他的任期内，

sentences.en: he has repeatedly impacted on government policy that in turn has had a knock-on effect on the material circumstances of the people living in Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 他屡次影响政府政策，而这反过来又对生活在白教堂的人们的物质环境产生了连锁反应。

sentences.en: So his first campaign, which he launched in 1883, it drew on a Congregationalist pamphlet titled The Bitter Cry of Outcast London.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在1883年发起的第一次活动，借鉴了一本名为《被遗忘的伦敦的痛苦呼喊》的公理会小册子。

sentences.en: He pushed this very, very hard to highlight the squalor and indignity and horror of London sluMs.
sentences.zh: 他非常非常努力地推动这一点，以突显伦敦贫民窟的肮脏、屈辱和恐怖。

sentences.en: And it played a massive role in encouraging the government to embark on the programme of slum clearance that by 1888 was kind of lapping at the borders of spittle fields and ironically had served to make lots of people homeless,
sentences.zh: 这在鼓励政府开展贫民窟清除计划方面发挥了巨大作用，该计划到1888年已经蔓延到了斯皮塔菲尔德的边缘，具有讽刺意味的是，这导致了许多人无家可归，

sentences.en: to displace people from their homes and had added to the overcrowding in Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 使人们流离失所，并加剧了白教堂的人口过剩。

sentences.en: So that's one way in which Stead has impacted on events in Florendine Street and Thrall Street and Dorset Street and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以这是斯特德对弗洛伦丁街、索罗街、多塞特街等地的事件产生影响的一种方式。

sentences.en: Then in 1885, he'd launched his most famous campaign, which we've already briefly mentioned.
sentences.zh: 然后在1885年，他发起了他最著名的活动，我们之前已经简要提到过。

sentences.en: And this was a series of four articles headlined The Maiden Tribute of Modern Babylon.
sentences.zh: 这是一系列四篇文章，头条是《现代巴比伦的处女贡》。

sentences.en: And it detailed how members of the British elite were preying on young working class girls, how these girls were, and I quote, snared, trapped and outraged.
sentences.zh: 其中详细描述了英国精英阶层的成员是如何捕食年轻的工人阶级女孩的，这些女孩是如何被——引述他的话说——诱捕、设局和凌辱的。

sentences.en: And Stead was kind of ramped up the horror of this in brilliantly melodramatic terMs.
sentences.zh: 斯特德用精彩的情节剧般的词藻，把这种恐怖气氛渲染到了极点。

sentences.en: So here he is.
sentences.zh: 所以他来了。

sentences.en: Do the girls cry out?
sentences.zh: 女孩们会哭喊吗？

sentences.en: Of course they do.
sentences.zh: 她们当然会。

sentences.en: But what avail screaming in a quiet bedroom?
sentences.zh: 但在安静的卧室里尖叫又有什么用呢？

sentences.en: And his most spectacular, his most notorious stunt was literally to buy a 13-year-old girl for £5 from her mother.
sentences.zh: 而他最轰动、最恶名昭彰的把戏，竟然真的是从一个母亲手里花了5英镑买下一个13岁的女孩。

sentences.en: Eliza Armstrong, her name was.
sentences.zh: 她叫伊莉莎·阿姆斯特朗。

sentences.en: Yeah, a massive scandal that he did this.
sentences.zh: 对，他做出这种事简直是个弥天大丑闻。

sentences.en: And he took her, didn't he, to, what did he take her to?
sentences.zh: 而且他把她带走了，对吧，带到了——他把她带到哪儿去了？

sentences.en: I can't remember where he took her.
sentences.zh: 我想不起来他把她带到哪里去了。

sentences.en: But he didn't do anything to her.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有对她做什么。

sentences.en: But the whole point of it was to demonstrate that it could be done.
sentences.zh: 但这件事的核心意义在于向世人证明这是做得到的。

sentences.en: And he actually ends up being prosecuted for it, which just kind of compounds the publicity effect of the whole campaign.
sentences.zh: 而且他最终居然因此被起诉，这反而进一步放大了整场运动的舆论效应。

sentences.en: And the impact of this is both immense and immediate.
sentences.zh: 其影响既深远又直接。

sentences.en: And it leads directly in the same year of 1885 to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, which is a very momentous piece of legislation.
sentences.zh: 并在同年（即1885年）直接促成了《刑事法修正案》，这是一部意义重大的立法。

sentences.en: So it rages the age of consent for girls from 13 to 16.
sentences.zh: 它将女孩的法定性承诺年龄从13岁提高到了16岁。

sentences.en: But it is also the act which led to the closure of brothels, which we mentioned in the first episode,
sentences.zh: 但这也是导致取缔妓院的法案——我们在第一集里提到过，

sentences.en: which had seen prostitutes evicted from their rooms and sent again out into Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 当时妓女被从房间里赶了出来，再次被流放到了白教堂街头。

sentences.en: So this, again, is part of what is making Whitechapel even more of a hotbed of overcrowding and vice than it had been before.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是导致白教堂地区比以往更加充斥着拥挤与罪恶的原因之一。

sentences.en: And just to add one other impact that it has, it makes gross indecency between male adults illegal.
sentences.zh: 为了补充它的另一个影响，它将成年男性之间的严重猥亵行为定为非法。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the so-called Laboucher Amendment, under which Oscar Wilde was convicted later on.
sentences.zh: 对，这就是所谓的“拉布歇修正案”，奥斯卡·王尔德后来就是在此罪名下被定罪的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and which I think will stay on the statute book until the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 对，而且我想这项法律一直保留在成文法典中，直到20世纪60年代。

sentences.en: Yeah, until 1967.
sentences.zh: 没错，直到1967年。

sentences.en: So it has a huge effect on the kind of the law governing sexual crimes in Britain.
sentences.zh: 因此，它对英国规范性犯罪的法律产生了巨大影响。

sentences.en: But it also has a massive influence on the cultural climate and it whips up a sense that aristocratic predators are everywhere, stalking working class girls.
sentences.zh: 但它也对文化气候产生了巨大影响，煽动起一种贵族掠食者无处不在、正伺机尾随工薪阶层女孩的情绪。

sentences.en: And there's a slight I think in terms of the obsession with it, there's perhaps a slight hint of kind of Jeffrey Epstein.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，就这种迷恋而言，其中或许还有点类似于杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的影子。

sentences.en: The kind of fascination of that case for people is the fact that his clients are all seen as being members of the elite princes and presidents and so on.
sentences.zh: 这起案件之所以让人如此着迷，是因为他的客户全都被视为精英阶层的王子、总统之流。

sentences.en: And it's massively amplified by reports in the Pall Mall Gazette in the years that follow of sex crimes that focus very,
sentences.zh: 而在接下来的几年里，《环球晚报》关于性犯罪的报道对这种情绪起到了巨大的放大作用，

sentences.en: very precisely on the iniquity of aristocrats and baronets and people like that.
sentences.zh: 非常精准地聚焦于贵族、从男爵以及这类人的罪恶。

sentences.en: Yeah, these are crimes carried out by people in top hats with kind of expensive suitcases who are whisking girls off to Paris and then outraging them.
sentences.zh: 对，这些罪行是由戴着大礼帽、拿着昂贵手提箱的人犯下的，他们把女孩拐到巴黎，然后对她们施暴。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the formula, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是他们的套路，对吧？

sentences.en: So these crimes, Stead is not interested in the Pall Mall Gazette is not interested in crimes of abuse or exploitation that are committed by people lower down the social spectrum,
sentences.zh: 所以这些罪行——斯特德对《环球晚报》并不感兴趣，他们对社会阶层较低的人所犯下的虐待或剥削罪行并不感兴趣，

sentences.en: particularly.
sentences.zh: 尤其是这样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, again, I mean, people are much more interested in what Prince Andrew did than, say, groomers and predators from, you know, in Britain who were not princes.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，人们对安德鲁王子所做的事的兴趣，远大于对英国那些并非王子的诱拐犯和恶魔的兴趣。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Stead is not interested basically in the grooming of of working class girls by working class men.
sentences.zh: 而且斯特德基本上对工薪阶层男性诱骗工薪阶层女孩并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And I think that had Stead come across the story of the upper class rate taking Mary Jane Kelly to Paris, he would have been all over it.
sentences.zh: 我想如果斯特德碰巧知道了某个上流社会败类把玛丽·简·凯利带到巴黎的故事，他一定会大肆炒作。

sentences.en: And it may be that, you know, that there was an aristocrat who had groomed and trafficked her.
sentences.zh: 也许——你知道的——确实有个贵族诱骗并贩卖了她。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们并不知道。

sentences.en: Stead is reporting things that did actually happen.
sentences.zh: 斯特德报道的都是确实发生过的事情。

sentences.en: But as you suggested, I think it's equally possible that Mary Jane, who's clearly very interested in newspaper reports and melodrama and stories of crime and so on,
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，我也觉得同样有一种可能是，玛丽·简显然对报纸报道、情节剧以及犯罪故事之类的内容非常感兴趣，

sentences.en: that she might have picked it up and kind of cast herself as the heroine of such a drama.
sentences.zh: 她可能自己也读过这些，并把想象中的自己当成了这种戏剧里的女主角。

sentences.en: And she's clearly not the only person picking this up, right?
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，不只是她一个人在关注这些，对吧？

sentences.en: Because I would argue that so much of the mystique of Jack, the so-called mystique, I mean, it's a terrible thing to say about somebody who committed such horrendous crimes,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为，关于“开膛手杰克”的神秘感——所谓的神秘感，对一个犯下如此恐怖罪行的人说这话实在太可怕了——

sentences.en: that so much of the mystique and the ill-gotten glamour of Jack the Ripper comes from this idea that he's a bloke in a top hat in a carriage,
sentences.zh: 这种神秘感以及开膛手杰克那不义的魅力，很大程度上来自于这样一个形象：一个坐在马车里、头戴大礼帽的家伙，

sentences.en: rattling down the streets of Whitechapel through the fog, seducing these young women and then, you know, venting his awful kind of passions on them.
sentences.zh: 在迷雾中穿梭于白教堂的街道，诱惑着这些年轻女性，然后——你知道的——把他人性中可怕的激情发泄在她们身上。

sentences.en: We're basically in W.T.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上是进入了W.T.

sentences.en: Stead's mental universe, right?
sentences.zh: 斯特德的精神世界，对吧？

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've had a couple of descriptions that exactly match that image.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们之前看过好几段完全符合这种形象的描述。

sentences.en: So there's the one with which we opened this episode.
sentences.zh: 比如我们这一集开头提到的那段。

sentences.en: And then, of course, the most famous is the description that Hutchinson gave, the very detailed account of the man that he'd seen talking to Mary Jane Kelly.
sentences.zh: 当然，最著名的还是哈钦森给出的描述，那是关于他曾看到与玛丽·简·凯利交谈的那名男子的极其详细的供述。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, the Astrakhan coat or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，那件紫羔皮大衣什么的。

sentences.en: Yeah, a couple of hours before her murder.
sentences.zh: 没错，就在她被谋杀前几个小时。

sentences.en: And it's a report that is taken very seriously by students of Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 这是一份被开膛手杰克的研究者们非常严肃对待的报告。

sentences.en: So as Philip Sugden puts it, Hutchinson has been widely described by students of the case as the witness most likely to have met Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 正如菲利普·萨格登所言，哈钦森被该案的研究者们广泛描述为“最有可能见过开膛手杰克”的目击者。

sentences.en: And this was certainly what Inspector Abbelein seems briefly to have hoped, because in the report that Hutchinson gave of the man that he had seen,
sentences.zh: 这当然也是阿伯莱因督察似乎短暂地抱有希望的原因，因为在哈钦森关于他所见男子的报告中，

sentences.en: there was this phrase, can be identified, right at the end.
sentences.zh: 最后有这样一句话：“此人可被辨认出来”，就在最末尾。

sentences.en: And you can imagine Abbelein's hopes soaring when he read that.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象阿伯莱因读到这里时内心的希望是如何高涨的。

sentences.en: It is evident that Abbelein had very quickly lost confidence in Hutchinson.
sentences.zh: 很显然，阿伯莱因很快就对哈钦森失去了信心。

sentences.en: And so people may wonder why.
sentences.zh: 所以大家可能会纳闷这是为什么。

sentences.en: So I think there are two possible theories.
sentences.zh: 我想这里有两种可能的理论。

sentences.en: So the first is given by Donald Rumbelow in his book, The Complete Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 第一种由唐纳德·鲁姆伯洛在他的书《完整的开膛手杰克》中提出。

sentences.en: And Rumbelow wrote, Hutchinson said the suspect lived in the area and thought that he had seen him in Petticoat Lane Market, so very close to the murder site, on a Sunday morning.
sentences.zh: 鲁姆伯洛写道，哈钦森称嫌疑人住在该地区，并认为在一个周日上午的 Petticoat Lane 市场——也就是离谋杀现场非常近的地方——见过他。

sentences.en: Possibly he did.
sentences.zh: 也许他确实见过。
